title: Choose the right coding task
scenario: You are not a programmer. You want AI help with something small, and you are deciding which kind of task fits what code generation actually does well on a first pass.
task: Pick the task that fits AI code generation well — as a draft to review.

options.text: Write a short script that renames every image in a folder to a numbered sequence — for me to review before use.
options.feedback: Small, precisely described, with checkable behavior and a review step built in — exactly the shape generation handles well.

options.text: Guarantee that our customer portal is secure against attacks.
options.feedback: Security work is verification-heavy and consequence-heavy — no tool can guarantee anything, and the checking is the actual job.

options.text: Find which line of our 40,000-line codebase causes a login bug that appears once a week.
options.feedback: It cannot see your codebase or run it. Diagnosing a live bug needs context, reproduction and inspection — AI can assist inside that process, not replace it.

options.text: Decide whether we should rebuild our checkout system or patch it.
options.feedback: An engineering and product judgment with long consequences — the kind of decision that stays human.

hints: Which task has a small, checkable outcome?
Which tasks ask for guarantees or judgment rather than a draft?
explanation: The four limits do the sorting: no guarantee, no context, no responsibility, uncertain freshness. Small draft-and-review tasks survive all four; guarantees, context-heavy debugging and product judgment run straight into them.
